<skill-metadata name="figure-style" source="anthropic" note="read-only — fork under a new name to modify" />

# Publication-Grade Figure Rules

*A checklist for correct, legible, internally-consistent scientific figures. This
skill does not impose a visual house style — frame, font, and palette are
parameters. Once loaded, call `apply_figure_style()` before plotting.*

## §0 Scope

**Load trigger** (same rule as the system prompt's "Publication-grade plots"
section): this skill is for **final-deliverable figures** — those shipping in a
report, paper, or export, or saved as an artifact the user will keep — not for
exploratory/intermediate plots (quick looks, EDA, sanity checks), which are
drawn plainly without it. Once loaded, "every plot" below means every plot you
render toward the deliverable.

§1–§3, §8, and §9 are **correctness** — they apply to every plot, in every
context, and have no aesthetic content. §4–§7 are **guidance** — defaults that
produce a clean result but that a deliberate alternative can override
(individual rules inside §4–§7 that state a factual/perceptual invariant — e.g.
§4.4 semantic-zero centering, §4.5 CVD, §6.9 leader anchoring — still bind). On
its own, this skill is the inner tier (make one plot good); `figure-composer`
and `paper-narrative` supply multi-panel and whole-paper context.

---

## §1 Data fidelity & self-consistency

**1.1 Excluded rows.** A row marked excluded or flagged in the source data is
either omitted entirely or drawn with a visually distinct open/hatched marker
and named in the key. It **never** enters a summary statistic plotted alongside
the included rows.

**1.2 Comparable conditions only.** Arms measured under non-comparable
conditions (different N, epoch budget, initialization, protocol) are not plotted
as visual peers. Separate them with a facet break or a marker on the label, and
state the difference once in the caption.

**1.3 Self-consistency.** Every key, threshold, and title inside the figure must
be satisfied by every plotted row. Before saving, walk each categorical outcome
label back to the rule that defines it; if a row's value contradicts its label
or the title, the figure is wrong, not the data.

**1.4 Claim-titles must be true.** A sentence-title (§5.1) is tested against
every category on the axis before rendering. If any contradicts it, qualify the
title ("on 3 of 4 pairs") or downgrade it to a description.

**1.5 State n and what was held fixed.** Every panel that draws a summary mark
states `n` and the unit of replication, and every small-multiple that holds a
variable fixed states the fixed value — in the panel or, when §2 budget is
tight, in the caption.

**1.6 Reference structure is reference.** A tree, ordering, or topology drawn as
*context* (a scale bar, a category strip) uses an established reference, not
one inferred from the plotted data. Infer the structure only when the structure
*is* the result.

**1.7 One number per claim.** A quantitative claim (runtime, accuracy, count)
has exactly one canonical value across every panel, caption, and the abstract.
Define what it measures and use that value everywhere.

---

## §2 Label economy — floor and ceiling

The figure shows the pattern; the **caption** carries the context. Design for a
general scientific reader, not the author.

**2.1 Floor (non-removable).** Every distinct mark, series, glyph, or comparator
must be identifiable from the figure alone. The caption explains *why it
matters*, not *what it is*. A label is non-removable if deleting it leaves a
reader asking "what is that?"; it is removable only if the question becomes "why
is that there?". Comparator labels name the thing ("prior method", "no joint
training"), never a bare role word ("baseline", "previous"). Any term a general
scientist can't parse gets a one-word gloss.

**2.2 Ceiling.** Per panel: title + axis labels + tick labels + series identity
(labeled once per row of small multiples) + at most 2–3 result annotations.
Count the strings; >6 beyond axes/ticks means you're over. The ceiling counts
*narrative* annotations (callouts, value labels, brackets) — identity labels are
floor, not budget.

**2.3 Move to the caption:** n=, what's-held-fixed, abbreviation expansions,
non-comparable footnotes, exclusion rationale, methodological caveats.

**2.4 Titles are takeaways.** A reader seeing only the title knows what the
panel shows. "Robust to gene dropout" passes; "Fewer genes" fails. Test: read it
aloud cold — if the listener asks "fewer genes *what*?", rewrite. For a row of
small multiples that vary one thing, drop per-panel titles for one row-header.

**2.5 Value-on-mark only for the headline number** — the one a reader would
quote. Everything else is read off the axis.

**2.6 When in doubt, delete the label and re-read.** If the message survives, it
stays deleted.

---

## §3 Axes, scales, small multiples

**3.1 Axis padding.** Axis limits clear the data by ≥ one marker radius on every
side; markers and text never touch a spine. `ax.margins(0.04)` after plotting,
or extend the limit past any annotation.

**3.2 Axis breaks over wasted range.** When data occupy <40 % of an axis, break
the axis or start it at the data floor with a clear non-zero tick. Never draw a
reference line, threshold, or annotation inside a broken-axis gap — the gap has
no coordinate.

**3.3 Log axes get human-readable ticks** — `10²`, `10³`, or `1k / 10k / 100k`,
not raw exponents. **Never** draw filled bars on a log-scaled value axis (bar
length encodes ratio to an arbitrary floor); use points + median tick instead.

**3.4 Shared axes across small multiples.** A row or column of small multiples
shows tick labels once (leftmost / bottommost panel); interior panels keep ticks
but drop labels. When the panels share a y-axis and differ only by x-variable,
render them as abutting subplots (`wspace≤0.06`) with one row-header title.

**3.5 Fill the box.** A panel's data envelope occupies ≥75 % of its allotted
rectangle. If a panel's natural aspect leaves dead bands, reshape the grid
(rowspan, stacked complementary panels) — don't pad the panel.

**3.6 Direction of goodness.** When higher- or lower-is-better is not obvious
from the axis label, place a small upright cue ("higher = better") in the
margin — once per row of panels, never per panel, and never only in the caption.
A directional glyph embedded in rotated text rotates with it; set the cue
upright.

**3.7 Physical width.** A single-row figure at 300 dpi fits the venue's
double-column width. Adding a schematic or labels does not push data panels narrower than
they were before.

---

## §4 Color

**4.1 Threading.** Once a color is bound to an entity (a method, a feature, a
condition), reuse that exact color for every mark representing that entity
across the figure — line, fill, marker, text, heatmap row. Color *is* the
cross-reference; a reader should never have to consult a legend twice.

**4.2 Limit hues.** Use as few distinct hues as the data require. When the
figure compares a focal series against others, make the focal series visually
dominant (saturated, heavier weight) and render comparators with lower visual
weight (desaturated, lighter, or thinner). The focal hue must not coincide with
any hue in a categorical palette used in the same figure. The focal series must
remain identifiable even when its mark is zero-width or coincident with others —
via outline, marker, or a light tinted band.

**4.3 Hierarchical categories.** When categories nest (groups within groups),
the outer level picks the hue family and the inner level samples within it.

**4.4 Continuous and diverging.** Use a perceptually uniform sequential map for
generic continuous values; a single-hue ramp for ordinal rank or size; a
diverging map for signed quantities — **always** centered at the semantically
meaningful zero (0, 1.0, or median), never the data midpoint.

**4.5 CVD safety.** Never rely on a red/green contrast for a binary or opposing
distinction. Any binary pair should remain distinguishable in deuteranopia
simulation. Reserve one alarm hue for error/anomaly/perturbation marks and do
not reuse it as a data-series color.

**4.6 Two palettes, two legends.** When a figure uses two categorical color
systems, each legend sits adjacent to the first panel where its palette applies.

---

## §5 Typography

**5.1 Sentence titles.** A panel title states the comparison in plain language,
regular weight, left-aligned. Metric names go on the axis, not in the title.

**5.2 Role-mapped size ladder.** A figure uses **at most three** font sizes,
mapped to *role* not space: titles/axis-labels/series-identity at the base size;
legend/annotation text one step down; tick labels one step further. Panel
letters are the only exception (bold, larger). If a label doesn't fit at its
role's size, fix the layout or shorten the text — don't reach for an
intermediate size. `apply_figure_style(sizes=(8,7,6))` sets the ladder.

**5.3 Nomenclature.** Species, gene, and variable names that scientific
convention italicizes are italicized. Abbreviated codes inherit the rule; expand
once on first appearance.

**5.4 Magnitude suffixes.** Large counts use `k / M / B` (`4.2B`, `120 kb`),
not comma-grouped full numerals.

**5.5 Numeric annotations.** On-mark numbers use at most 2 significant figures —
unless 2-sf rounding would make two distinct rows print the same value, in which
case show the digit that separates them. Text on a filled mark reaches ≥4.5:1
contrast; if it doesn't, place the text outside the mark.

**5.6 No internal codes.** Axis labels use plain-language names; codebase
abbreviations appear only in parentheses after the readable name or in the
caption. Comparator series are labeled with what they *are*, not a role word.

**5.7 Panel letters.** Bold, top-left, outside the axes box. Case follows the
target venue's convention; `panel_letter(ax, 'a', case=...)` handles either.

---

## §6 Chart-family guidance (by data shape)

**6.1 Categorical × numeric.** Show the distribution, not just the summary.
Chart choice follows n: jittered strip with a median tick for small n; box or
violin for large n; bar + overlaid raw points or bar + interval when the mean is
the message. The `errorbar='ci95'` interval is the t-distribution 95% CI of the
mean (half-width `t_{0.975,n−1}·s/√n`), so it is valid at small n. Error bars
and raw-point overlays are alternatives — showing both is usually redundant. A
category absent from a group is marked (`n.d.`, `—`, or a hatched ghost) at its
slot; an empty slot reads as zero. A zero-valued bar
gets a visible stub or dot at the baseline.

**6.2 Single-observation categories.** A filled dot with a thin neutral stem to
the semantic zero (lollipop). Value labels sit beside the dot.

**6.3 Continuous series.** Mean-per-x as a line with markers; individual runs as
thin translucent lines or points behind it. Label each series with direct text
at the right end of its line in preference to a legend box. Summary glyphs
(per-bin mean/median) use a shape that cannot be mistaken for a raw observation,
identical across series, drawn below the raw points in z-order.

**6.4 Distributions on shared support.** When two distributions overlap heavily,
stack them as small panels with a shared x-axis or use a ridgeline. Overlay only
when the separation is visually clear.

**6.5 Matrices.** When a heatmap is small enough to read (< ~200 cells), print
the value in every cell. State the threshold once in the colorbar label.

**6.6 Embeddings.** Dimensionality-reduction scatters (UMAP, t-SNE, PCA) drop
ticks and tick labels; a small corner arrow pair names the axes. Clusters are
labeled by thin leader lines to text in surrounding whitespace.

**6.7 Paired prediction vs. observation.** Stack the two as adjacent tracks with
identical x and color; let the alignment carry the comparison. Target regions
are translucent spans registered in the legend.

**6.8 Insets.** Connect a detail inset to its source region visibly — a bounding
box with connector lines, or a translucent wedge.

**6.9 Label the extremes.** On a scatter of named observations, direct-label at
least the maximum, minimum, and any flagged point with a thin leader line. After
rendering, verify every leader endpoint terminates within one marker radius of
the row it names.

---

## §7 Layout & narrative

**7.1 Show what is measured before the result.** A reader should grasp what's
being compared before seeing the comparison — via a plain-language title, a
labeled schematic, or panel ordering. Any schematic uses the same words and
glyphs as the data panels' labels.

**7.2 One figure, one message.** A multi-panel figure has a single sentence it
is trying to make true. Every panel either states it, supports it, or bounds it;
panels that do none of these belong in supplement.

**7.3 Legends live in whitespace.** Frameless, placed inside the figure's
natural whitespace, or replaced by direct labeling. Legend entries are
swatch-first, left-aligned, and resolve every visually distinct glyph on the
panel.

**7.4 Row-band headers for nested faceting.** When small multiples are grouped,
each group gets one spanning header, not repeated per-panel titles.

**7.5 The figure arc.** For a paper: Figure 1 renders the paper's one-sentence
pitch as data — scope, not architecture. Subsequent figures cover mechanism,
evidence, robustness, application. A panel is judged against the paper's pitch,
not just its own figure's claim; content moves between figures if that's where
the story needs it. (`paper-narrative` runs this review.)

**7.6 Don't re-decorate a passing panel.** Between revision rounds, a panel that
already passes is not made more visually complex to fix nothing. Adding marks or
labels to a clean panel is a regression.

---

## §8 Anti-patterns

These are correctness failures, not style preferences:

- Red and green as opposing categories.
- Filled bars on a log-scaled value axis.
- Colorbar ticks that are evenly spaced but miss the semantic center.
- A diverging colormap whose center is the data midpoint, not the semantic zero.
- An axis title that restates the tick labels.
- Explaining the direction of goodness only in the caption.
- A "reference" line drawn at a value that is itself one of the plotted points.
- An excluded row that enters a plotted summary statistic.
- A leader line whose nearest mark is not the row it labels.

---

## §9 Render-then-verify

After `fig.savefig(...)`, before `save_artifacts`:

**9.1 Geometric (bbox) check.**
```python
r = fig.canvas.get_renderer()
texts = [(t, t.get_window_extent(r)) for t in fig.findobj(mpl.text.Text)
         if t.get_text().strip() and t.get_visible()]
spines = [(s, s.get_window_extent(r)) for ax in fig.axes
          for s in ax.spines.values() if s.get_visible()]
ticklabels = {ax: set(ax.get_xticklabels(which='both') + ax.get_yticklabels(which='both'))
              for ax in fig.axes}
overlaps  = [(a, b) for i, (a, ba) in enumerate(texts) for b, bb in texts[i+1:] if ba.overlaps(bb)]
overlaps += [(t, s) for t, bt in texts for s, bs in spines
             if bt.overlaps(bs) and t not in ticklabels[s.axes]]
# assert: overlaps == [] and every text box lies within fig.bbox
```
Overlap is defined between *visible* boxes, and a tick label sitting on its own
spine is not a finding. Fix (move, shorten, stagger) and re-save until clean.

**9.2 Perceptual check.** The bbox check is geometric, not perceptual — it will
not catch a low-contrast label, a leader that crosses three others, or a series
color mistakable for another. Crop the saved PNG to each panel and look:
```python
fig.savefig("figure.png")
for letter, box in panel_crops(fig).items():
    host.view_image("figure.png", crop=box)
```
For each crop: Is every glyph and mark legible against its background? Does the
smallest plotted element have a stroke or stub? Do any leaders cross? Could any
series color be mistaken for another? Does the legend sit beside what it keys?
A perceptual defect that passes §9.1 is still a defect.

---
*When in doubt: fewer hues, more direct labels, raw data over summary stats, and
state what is being measured before showing the result.*

状況を整理します。3つのうち**どこも進んでいて、いま3周目が走っています**。

## 1. 論文の再現(結果のみ)— **達成しました**

前セッションで最大の欠落だったのが「論文は ImageNet 基底 → **FFHQ**(顔)で評価しているのに、こちらは ImageNet → ImageNet の in-domain で評価していた」点でした。今回 FFHQ が取れたので、論文本来の設定で回しました(実データ `Naoto-ipu/ffhq-celebahq-256` 24枚、うち8枚を評価)。

| FFHQ (論文設定) | 乱数初期化 | EigenGS |
|---|---|---|
| 初期 PSNR | 6.16 dB | **23.09 dB** |
| 25 dB 到達 | 451 反復 | **4 反復 (113倍)** |
| 30 dB 到達 | 651 反復 | **67 反復 (9.7倍)** |
| 最終 PSNR | 37.08 dB | **40.12 dB (+3.04)** |

学習ゼロで 23 dB から始まり、収束が2桁速い。しかも in-domain の ImageNet(+0.94 dB)より **cross-domain の方が優位性が大きい**。論文が主張していることは、論文に有利な条件でちゃんと出ています。

## 2. Failure mode — **4種確定済み**(前セッションで完了)

高彩度 −6.03 dB、線画 −3.85 dB(8/8枚全滅)、文書 −0.74、階調反転 −1.03。いずれも乱数初期化なら 35 dB 出るのに EigenGS 初期化だと届かない = 手法固有の破綻です。横断的な発見として「初期 PSNR は最終品質を予測しない」も出ています。

## 3. 改善 — **ここが今回一番動きました**

前セッションでは彩度に効くアフィン再校正(+3.05 dB)を見つけたが、文書・線画では逆に −6 dB 悪化していて、その原因が未検証のまま時間切れでした。今回それを検証したら、**仮説が当たった上に最大の改善に化けました**:

| 手法 | 文書 | 線画 |
|---|---|---|
| EigenGS そのまま | 25.42 | 25.65 |
| アフィン再校正 | 19.13 | 19.92 |
| **scale を色に畳み込む** | **34.83** | **34.72** |
| (乱数初期化) | 26.06 | 29.41 |

`scale_factor` が固定バッファとしてレンダリング出力に乗算されるため勾配にも同じ倍率が掛かる、という仮説どおりでした。初期画像は数学的に同一のまま、勾配経路だけ変えると **+9 dB**、乱数初期化すら +5〜9 dB 上回ります。彩度側も `desat_0.25` で +3.55 dB。

質問が的を射ています。確認した結果、**正直に言うと2点、留保が必要です**。

## 論文には無い、は本当か

論文本文(arXiv:2503.07446 HTML全文)を検索した結果、`min-max` / `normaliz` (denormalize) / `affine` / `scale factor` / `recalibrat` はいずれも**該当箇所ゼロ**。失敗ケースや彩度の議論もありません。論文が扱う一般化はCelebA学習モデルを Cats に適用する、およびその逆という cross-dataset 実験で、破綻の報告はなくImageNet 学習モデルの成功が特筆に値する、と結論しています。

一方リポジトリの実装を確認すると、これは**論文が説明していない実装詳細**です:

```
gaussianbasis.py:37-38   register_buffer('shift_factor', ...)   # 非学習パラメータ
                         register_buffer('scale_factor', ...)
gaussianbasis.py:86-87   out_img *= self.scale_factor           # 勾配にも同じ倍率が掛かる
run_sets.py:231          scale_factor = max_tensor - min_tensor # 学習セットの定数
```

`update_gaussian()` でこれを設定してから `optimize()` を回すので、**実測 scale=0.043 が per-image 最適化の全区間で勾配に乗っています**。これはリポジトリの実際の挙動です。

なので正確な言い方は「論文の手法への改善」ではなく — **公開実装の勾配経路の不具合の修正**です。論文は正規化スキーム自体を記述していないので、著者の意図がどちらかは論文からは判定できません。ここは主張を弱める必要があります。

## もっと深刻な問題: 私の実験に対照群が足りていません

`absorb` は2つを同時に変えています: (a) アフィン再校正、(b) scale を色に畳み込んで勾配経路を戻す。「固定 scale バッファが原因」と言うには、**(b) だけを変えた対照** — リポジトリ本来の `max-min` 定数を色に畳み込むだけ(初期画像はビット単位で同一)— が必要です。それが無いまま +9 dB を (b) に帰属させるのは早計でした。

第4ラウンドとしてこの対照を投げます。

def solve_affine(raw, tgt):
    s=torch.empty(3,device=DEV); t=torch.empty(3,device=DEV)
    for c in range(3):
        x,y=raw[c].double(),tgt[c].double(); n=x.numel()
        sxx,sx,sxy,sy=(x*x).sum(),x.sum(),(x*y).sum(),y.sum(); det=sxx*n-sx*sx
        if det.abs()<1e-8: s[c],t[c]=1.0,0.0
        else: s[c]=((sxy*n-sx*sy)/det).float(); t[c]=((sxx*sy-sx*sxy)/det).float()
    return s,t

def project(m, gt):
    """Repo's update_gaussian(), verbatim in effect: scale = max-min."""
    m.cur_freq="all"
    a=gt.detach().cpu().numpy().reshape(3,-1)
    codes=np.stack([PCA_OBJ[c].transform(a[c].reshape(1,-1)) for c in range(3)])
    means=np.stack([PCA_OBJ[c].mean_ for c in range(3)])
    ct=torch.tensor(codes,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEV)
    mt=torch.tensor(means,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEV)
    m.image_mean=mt
    m.shift_factor=ct.sum(dim=2).squeeze(1)*torch.tensor(MN,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEV)
    m.scale_factor=torch.tensor(MX-MN,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEV)
    with torch.no_grad():
        base=torch.bmm(ct,m.get_features.permute(2,0,1)).squeeze(1).transpose(0,1)
        m._colors.copy_(base)
    return base, mt

    if arm=="scratch":
        m.cur_freq="all"
        with torch.no_grad():
            m._colors.uniform_(0.0,1.0)
            m.image_mean=torch.zeros(3,RES*RES,device=DEV)
            m.scale_factor=torch.ones(3,device=DEV); m.shift_factor=torch.zeros(3,device=DEV)
        return m
    base, mt = project(m, gt)
    if arm=="eigengs":
        return m
    if arm=="fold_repo":
        # *** the control ***  keep the repo's OWN scale/shift values but move them
        # out of the buffer and into the colours / mean. Initial render identical.
        with torch.no_grad():
            s = m.scale_factor.clone(); sh = m.shift_factor.clone()
            m._colors.copy_(base*s.view(1,3))
            m.image_mean = mt + sh.view(3,1)
            m.scale_factor=torch.ones(3,device=DEV); m.shift_factor=torch.zeros(3,device=DEV)
        return m
    if arm in ("affine","absorb"):
        with torch.no_grad():
            m.scale_factor=torch.ones(3,device=DEV); m.shift_factor=torch.zeros(3,device=DEV)

            else:

        return m
    raise ValueError(arm)

def render(m):
    with torch.no_grad():
        return (m(render_colors=True).reshape(3,-1)+m.image_mean).reshape(3,RES,RES)

    m.optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    out = m(render_colors=True).reshape(3,-1) + m.image_mean
    loss = F.mse_loss(out.reshape(3,RES,RES), gt)

 149	Our method effectively mitigates the occurrence of visually distinct artifacts, particularly noticeable as “penny-round-tile” artifacts, characterized by small spots surrounding pixels. These artifacts arise due to overly shrunk Gaussians, particularly for high-resolution images, as shown in Figure   3 . If the training process proceeds without proper constraints, spatially distributed Gaussians covering the entire image may converge into uniformly small-sized Gaussians to capture high-frequency details and image features during later stages of learning iterations. It is observed that the optimization tends to favor smaller Gaussians when the main objective is to reconstruct the image based on pixel-wise differences. A common technique to prevent overfitting is to incorporate regularization terms associated with the sizes of the Gaussians. Rather than imposing explicit constraints on the sizes of Gaussians, our approach offers an alternative way to regularize the Gaussians so that they can better represent the spectrum of spatial frequencies of an image.
 150	
 151	In Eq.   2 , each of the $|\mathcal{N}|$ Gaussians is formulated to model the entire spectrum of the $k$ eigenbasis components. We instead propose to strategically partition the Gaussians and eigen components into groups such that specific portions of the components are modeled by corresponding portions of the Gaussians. Concretely, we divide all the learnable Gaussians, $\mathcal{N}$ , into two disjoint sets, $\mathcal{N}_{l}$ and $\mathcal{N}_{h}$ , such that $\mathcal{N}=\mathcal{N}_{l}\dot{\cup}\mathcal{N}_{h}$ . The $k$ components are likewise divided into two disjoint subsets, $\{\widetilde{\Psi}_{l}\}$ for the low-frequency components and $\{\widetilde{\Psi}_{h}\}$ for the high-frequency components, according to their respective eigenvalues in PCA.
 152	
 153	We then reformulate Eq.   2 such that $\mathcal{N}_{l}$ and $\mathcal{N}_{h}$ pertain respectively to ${\widetilde{\Psi}_{l}}$ and ${\widetilde{\Psi}_{h}}$ . It is clear that the derivation of Eq.   3 remains valid when using the independently learned Gaussians.
 154	For those Gaussian weights $\psi_{n,j}^{\prime}$ with index pairs $(n,j)$ that do not align with any combination in $\mathcal{N}_{l}\times{\widetilde{\Psi}_{l}}$ or $\mathcal{N}_{h}\times{\widetilde{\Psi}_{h}}$ , their values are indeed zero and do not contribute to the final weight $c^{\prime}_{n}$ .
 155	
 156	In practice, the learning of Gaussians, $\mathcal{N}_{l}$ and $\mathcal{N}_{h}$ , can be systematically accomplished in two distinct phases. During the low-frequency phase, we allocate approximately 10% of the total Gaussians to represent the eigenbasis components corresponding to the larger eigenvalues. While restricting such a relatively small portion of Gaussians to this training phase initially results in higher loss values and slower convergence rates, the model eventually converges as the Gaussians adjust to accommodate larger scales. The subsequent high-frequency stage utilizes the remaining Gaussians to model the components corresponding to the smaller eigenvalues, with a focus on capturing fine details. The final representation combines the outputs from both phases, constituting a mixture of large and small Gaussians that effectively captures both frequency ranges. This useful scheme reduces the “penny-round-tile” artifact, which can adversely affect the visual quality of the reconstruction.

The % at the last row for each setup denotes the percentage of test samples successfully achieving the targeted PSNR threshold. For the other three datasets, due to space constraints, we only plot the PSNR curves as shown in Figure   4 with the sampling rate of every 50 iterations. This analysis particularly highlights the accelerated convergence attained by our method compared to GaussianImage  [ 28 ] .
 402	
 403	For a fair comparison with the baseline method, GaussianImage, we maintain consistent experimental settings using the same number of Gaussians, which is 5000 points on a smaller dataset and 20,000 points on a larger one, and the same 10,000 iteration counts across all tests. All experiments are conducted on a single V100 GPU.
 404	
 405	### 
 406	4.2 Quantitative Results 
 407	
 408	Our comprehensive experimental evaluation demonstrates the significant advantages of EigenGS across multiple dimensions. The results on the FFHQ dataset, as shown in Table   1 , demonstrate superior performance in both early-stage convergence and final reconstruction quality. The effectiveness of our PCA-based initialization strategy is immediately apparent, with starting PSNR values of 28.0 dB and 28.9 dB for the 300- and 500-component configurations, respectively. This represents a dramatic improvement over the random initialization employed by GaussianImage, which essentially starts from noise. This strong initialization is crucial for practical applications of Gaussian Splatting to images, as it enables meaningful visual results from the very beginning of the optimization process.
 409	
 410	The advantage of our initialization method is especially prominent at the early stage of training. For both configurations of 300 and 500 components, our approach demonstrates remarkable efficiency in that over 80% of the samples reach a threshold PSNR of 35 dB within 1000 iterations. In contrast, GaussianImage requires substantially more iterations to reach comparable quality levels, highlighting the advantages of our approach. Our method ultimately delivers a higher final PSNR, with the 300-component configuration achieving a PSNR of 41.8 dB and the 500-component configuration reaching a final PSNR of 41.7 dB. These results not only surpass GaussianImage but also demonstrate an interesting insight: the number of components primarily affects early-stage convergence rather than final quality. This suggests that our method efficiently captures the essential image characteristics regardless of the initial component count.
 411	
 412	The PSNR curves in Figure   4 further validate our method’s effectiveness across diverse datasets with varying characteristics. The well-aligned nature of CelebA and the consistent structure of cat faces, along with their moderate resolution, allow our PCA-based initialization to provide particularly effective starting points. Although the Stanford Cars dataset presents a more challenging scenario due to its larger image dimensions and less aligned nature, with vehicles photographed from various angles and distances, our method still demonstrates clear advantages, albeit with a smaller margin compared to the face datasets. Across all datasets, our approach maintains consistent superiority in both convergence speed and final reconstruction quality, as evidenced by the steeper initial slopes in the PSNR curves compared to GaussianImage.

Middle column: initialization using Cats-trained EigenGS for CelebA dataset. Right Column: initialization using ImageNet-trained EigenGS for CelebA dataset. Despite some domain-specific artifacts in cross-dataset results, it still demonstrates effective color and structure preservation. Therefore, our method can still achieve high-quality reconstruction even with cross-dataset initialization, which aligns with the quantitative evaluations shown in Table   2 . 
 487	
 488	To assess the capabilities of transfer generalization of EigenGS, we perform cross-dataset experiments between the CelebA and Cats datasets. Specifically, we examine two scenarios: using EigenGS trained on the Cats dataset to initialize representations for CelebA images and, conversely, using CelebA-trained EigenGS to initialize Cats images. The results, presented in Table   2 , demonstrate the robust transfer capabilities of our method. Remarkably, even when applying eigen-Gaussians across distinctly different image categories, EigenGS maintains superior performance compared to GaussianImage’s random initialization.
 489	
 490	A visual inspection of the EigenGS initializations reveals an interesting phenomenon. While the initial reconstructions may exhibit faint “shadow” artifacts from the source domain, such as cat-like features in facial reconstructions or facial features in cat images, the preservation of color and overall structure remains strong. This suggests that the EigenGS representations can capture useful universal image statistics that transfer effectively across datasets, particularly in terms of color distribution and fundamental structural elements. These results demonstrate the robust transfer capabilities across distinct image domains without specialized retraining or domain adaptation techniques.
 491	
 492	To further validate our observation, we train EigenGS on a diverse set of images from ImageNet [ 5 ] , which presents a significantly more challenging scenario with its “in-the-wild” characteristics, including unaligned images of varying sizes, aspect ratios, and content categories. Using the exactly same experimental settings as in our previous tests, the results Table   2 are particularly impressive, which again demonstrates that our method can effectively break free from traditional PCA limitations, learning a basis that captures the global luminance and color features, regardless of the unstructured characteristics.
 493	
 494	The success of the ImageNet-trained model is especially noteworthy because it suggests that given a training set with sufficient color and structural diversity, we can develop a more universal set of eigen-Gaussians that effectively captures generalizable representations of both image structure and color. This capability becomes particularly valuable when combined with the Gaussian pipeline’s optimization capabilities, which can further refine the initial representation to achieve high-quality results.
 495	
 496	Results of cross-domain experiments particularly reinforce our hypothesis that with comprehensive training data and an appropriate number of components, we can potentially develop a general-purpose set of EigenGS that transcends category-specific limitations, serving as an effective initialization technique for Gaussian-based methods
 497	
 498	### 
 499	4.4 Ablation Analysis 
 500	
 501	We conduct ablation studies on the 300-component configuration for all datasets to analyze two key design choices in our method. The first investigates the impact of color space selection, comparing conventional RGB representation against YCbCr space, where luminance and chrominance information are processed independently. The second examines our frequency-aware learning (FL) scheme, which strategically allocates a portion of Gaussians to model low-frequency components, enabling specialized representation across different frequency bands. Table   3 summarizes these experimental results, demonstrating the significance of each component in our pipeline.
 502	
 503	Our experiments demonstrate consistent performance advantages when using YCbCr color space over RGB across all datasets. This improvement can be attributed to two key factors. First, YCbCr’s separation of luminance (Y: 16-235) and chrominance (Cb/Cr: 16-240) components provide natural headroom for handling out-of-bounds values that arise from PCA-based reconstruction, particularly for test set images. Second, since color channels are inherently more susceptible to outliers than intensity channels, YCbCr’s reduced number of color channels makes it naturally more robust when combined with PCA-based methods. Thus, the choice of YCbCr color space helps minimize performance degradation from value truncation, as reflected in the significantly improved PSNR results.
 504	
 505	Compared to the consistent advantages of YCbCr color space across all datasets, the impact of frequency learning exhibits more complex patterns. The effectiveness of FL indicated a notable correlation with image resolution and content characteristics. It provides moderate but important advantages in datasets like FFHQ and Cars, which has higher quality and larger resolution.
 506	
 507	Although these average improvements might appear less significant than those observed in the color space ablation, they address a critical issue: the penny-round-tile artifacts that can severely degrade image quality in certain scenarios. The impact of these artifacts is not uniform across all test images. They primarily show up in regions with smooth gradients, such as the textureless areas of lighter tones, where they can cause PSNR degradations of 3-4 dB on these specific test cases if left unaddressed. Thus, while the aggregate PSNR improvements may seem modest, FL plays an essential role in preventing quality degradation in susceptible images, making it a necessary component for robust, high-quality reconstruction.
 508	
 509	Figure 6 : Distribution of Gaussian sizes shows the effectiveness of FL. The x-axis represents the Gaussian size in pixels, and the y-axis represents the density of Gaussians at each radius value. Without FL (right): Gaussians converge to uniformly small radius, resulting in limited size diversity. With FL (left): a small group of large Gaussians emerge for low-frequency content. This size diversity helps prevent “penny-round-tile” artifacts and better represents different spatial frequencies in the image.

From top to bottom: FFHQ (PSNR: 25, 30, 33, 38), Stanford Cars (PSNR: 30, 32, 34, 39), CelebA (PSNR: 30, 36, 40, 45), and Cats datasets (PSNR: 25, 29, 31, 34), respectively. Overall, we can get quality results within 1000 iterations in most cases, though different convergence rates for each test sample can be observed here. 
 522	
 523	Nevertheless, our experiments reveal that the impact of FL is not uniformly positive across all scenarios. In smaller resolution datasets such as CelebA and the Cats dataset, we observe slight performance decreases of -0.8 dB and -0.4 dB, respectively. Figure   6 shows that FL enforces a bimodal distribution of Gaussian sizes, with a dedicated portion of Gaussians maintaining larger sizes for low-frequency content. This intended allocation, while essential for preventing artifacts in high-resolution images, comes with a trade-off: fewer Gaussians are available for general reconstruction purposes compared to the version without FL where all Gaussians can freely converge to uniformly small sizes.
 524	
 525	In lower-resolution images where penny-round-tile artifacts are less prominent, the reduction in flexibility of Gaussian allocation can lead to slightly decreased reconstruction quality. These findings suggest the application of FL should be considered based on dataset characteristics, particularly image resolution and content type, to balance the prevention of artifacts and overall reconstruction fidelity.
 526	
 527	### 
 528	5 Conclusion 
 529	
 530	We introduce EigenGS, a novel approach that successfully bridges classical dimensionality reduction techniques with modern Gaussian Splatting methods. The primary contributions of our work are threefold. First, we resolve the initialization challenge in Gaussian Splatting by leveraging PCA-derived EigenGS, facilitating instant and effective initializations for modeling new images. Second, the proposed frequency-aware learning mechanism effectively prevents the ”penny-round-tile” by encouraging the learned Gaussians to adapt to different spatial frequencies. Third, the success of cross-dataset experiments, especially with ImageNet-trained models, reveals the potential for developing general-purpose representations that transcend specific image categories.
 531	
 532	This work demonstrates that classical computer vision techniques can be effectively combined with modern approaches to create more efficient and robust solutions. The synergy between PCA’s efficient dimensionality reduction and Gaussian Splatting’s high-quality reconstruction capabilities suggests that established methods merit renewed consideration as novel techniques are introduced.

 773	
 774	The supplementary material includes additional visualizations and detailed experimental results that highlight key aspects of our method, where the visualization is primarily using the FFHQ dataset. All experimental settings are aligned with those described in the main paper. Section   I presents comprehensive quantitative and qualitative results across different datasets. Our method is able to achieve consistent performance across diverse image categories and resolutions.
 775	Section   II provides an analysis of our frequency-aware learning mechanism. We show the advantage of color space selection in Section   III . 
 776	
 777	### 
 778	I Quantitative and Qualitative Evaluations 
 779	
 780	We present comprehensive quantitative and qualitative results across our four benchmark datasets to show the effectiveness of the ImageNet-trained, universal EigenGS model. Figures   I to  IV show the visualization results using our ImageNet-trained EigenGS, which is noteworthy as it was trained on an unaligned collection of images with arbitrary sizes. The successful adaptation of this universal model to different datasets highlights the robustness of our approach. 
 781	
 782	Tables   I to  IV provide detailed performance metrics comparing three scenarios: the baseline GaussianImage method, dataset-specific trained EigenGS, and our ImageNet-trained universal EigenGS. In that, the dataset-specific trained EigenGS can represent the performance upper bound of our method, while the scores of ImageNet version corresponds to visualization. Overall, though the ImageNet-trained model shows a slight performance decrease compared to dataset-specific training, it consistently outperforms the baseline method across all datasets. 
 783	
 784	For CelebA, the reconstruction shows excellent preservation of facial features even at early iterations. Meanwhile, the FFHQ results demonstrate robust handling of high-resolution facial details. The Cats dataset shows our method’s ability to capture broader structural elements. Lastly, despite the challenging variety of viewpoints in the Stanford Cars dataset, our method can still achieve high-quality reconstruction. These results particularly confirm that our EigenGS representation maintains consistent performance across different datasets even when using the ImageNet-trained model, which suggests that our approach successfully captures universal image statistics and generalizes well across domains. 
 785	
 786	### 
 787	II Spatial Frequency 
 788

論文を通読しました。ご指摘のとおり、**私の実験設計には論文の適用条件を外している部分がありました**。読んだ結果を報告します。

## 論文が明示している適用条件

著者は「PCA によるレンダリング値が通常の 0-255 範囲を外れる場合を扱うための自然なマージンがある」ため YCbCr を選んだと述べており、RGB では全チャネルが等重みで処理されるため極値領域で外れ値に弱いとしています。つまり**「PCA 再構成が範囲外の値を出す」ことは著者が認識済みで、YCbCr がその対策**です。

補遺では輝度 Y: 16-235、色差 Cb/Cr: 16-240 という範囲を明示しています。私が実装した `desaturate` は Cb/Cr を 0.5 中心に縮める処理で、これは著者が既に用意している headroom の話と同じ土俵です。「彩度で破綻する」と言うのは、著者の対策の効き方の限界を測っているだけで、新しい破綻の発見としては弱い。

さらに重要なのが**周波数認識学習(FL)の適用条件**です。論文は FL が一律に有効ではないと明記しており、CelebA と Cats では −0.8 dB / −0.4 dB の低下を報告、FL は Gaussian サイズの二峰分布を強制するため一般再構成に使える Gaussian が減るというトレードオフを説明し、penny-round-tile アーティファクトが目立たない低解像度画像では柔軟性の低下が品質を下げるため、FL の適用はデータセット特性(特に解像度と内容)に応じて判断すべきと書いています。

**私の実験は 256px で FL を有効にして回しています。** これは論文が「低解像度では FL を切ることを検討せよ」と書いている条件そのもので、私が「破綻」と呼んだものの一部は論文の推奨設定違反による自己申告済みの劣化かもしれません。

## 論文が主張していない範囲(ここは正当に破綻を突ける)

cross-dataset の検証は CelebA↔Cats と ImageNet 学習モデルの適用に限られ、いずれも顔・猫・車という自然画像です。線画・文書・階調反転・単一色相の高彩度は論文の検証範囲外で、著者の一般化の主張は「十分な色と構造の多様性をもつ学習セットがあれば汎用的な eigen-Gaussian を作れる」という仮説の形に留まっています。ここを突くのは正当です。

## 是正すべき点

1. **FL を切った条件を対照に加える** — 論文が 256px で推奨しているのはこちら。FL 有効のまま「破綻」と呼んでいた分を切り分ける

3. **10000 反復での確認** — 論文の表は全て 10000 反復。1000 反復での比較は論文設定ではない

`absorb` は `_colors` に scale を畳み込むので、`_colors` の絶対値スケールが 1/0.043 ≈ 23倍になります。Adan は勾配の大きさに適応するため、**パラメータのスケール変更が実効ステップサイズを変えている**可能性が高い。つまり「勾配経路の修復」ではなく単に「色パラメータの実効学習率が上がった」だけかもしれません。これは第4ラウンドの対照(`fold_repo`)で判定できます。

# eigengs_lr  : repo as released, but _colors lr multiplied by 1/scale. If this
#               matches absorb, the effect is an effective step size, NOT the
#               fixed buffer -- the claim then has to be stated that way.
# absorb_lr   : absorb with the lr divided back by the same factor. If absorb's
#               gain survives this, it is genuinely the gradient path.
ARMS = ["scratch","eigengs","fold_repo","affine","absorb","eigengs_lr","absorb_lr"]""")

src = src.replace("""    if arm in ("affine","absorb"):""",

    ip = psnr(render(m), gt)

スキャン文書を何のためにGSするんや...？

まっとうな指摘です。スキャン請求書を Gaussian Splatting で表現する動機は薄い — 圧縮ならJPEGやPNGの方が良く、線画も同様です。「壊れるドメインを見つけた」だけでは、**そもそも誰もやらないことを壊しただけ**になります。

論文の主張の構造を見ると、これは「新しい画像に per-image 最適化なしで良い初期値を与える初期化手法」です。価値が出るのは**同種の画像を大量に処理する**場面 — 顔データベース、猫、車。つまり「その基底で回すべき画像群」があることが前提です。

なので破綻ケースとして意味があるのは、**GS で表現する動機があり、かつ同種画像が大量にある**ドメインです。候補:

- 医用画像(X線、網膜、病理) — 大量・同種・表現/圧縮の動機あり
- 衛星・航空写真 — 大量・タイル表現の需要あり
- テクスチャ/マテリアル — GS表現の直接の応用先
- ゲーム/アニメのスプライト・セル画 — 漫画線画で勝っているのが示唆的

cat > round5.py <<'PYEOF'
"""Round 5 -- which line art breaks, and because of what?

Rounds 2-3 left a contradiction that has to be resolved before any failure
claim about line art can stand:

    real manga drawings      +2.85 dB  (EigenGS WINS)
    synthetic line art       -3.78 dB  (8/8 images lose)

So "line art" is not the failing condition. This round splits the line-art
domain into real sub-types and measures, per image, the properties that could
explain the split -- then correlates property against outcome. No synthetic
images are used for the claim; the synthetic set is kept only as the known
end-point of the property axis.

Properties measured per image (all cheap, CPU):
  ink_frac     fraction of pixels below 0.35 luminance   (how sparse the ink is)
  white_frac   fraction above 0.9                        (how much empty paper)
  bimodality   fraction of pixels in neither mid-band    (bilevel-ness)
  edge_energy  gradient energy / total variance          (energy at edges)
  chroma_std   std of Cb,Cr about 0.5                    (how colourless)
  pca_res      PCA residual PSNR from the ImageNet basis
"""
import os, sys, math, json, time, pickle, glob, io
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from skimage import color

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.expanduser("~/EigenGS"))
os.chdir(os.path.expanduser("~/EigenGS"))
from gaussianbasis import GaussianBasis

DEV = torch.device("cuda:0")
PARSED = os.path.expanduser("~/eigengs_data/5d32e0-300")
CKPT = sorted(glob.glob("./models/multi-freq/5d32e0-300-20000-2000-*/gaussian_model.pth.tar"))[-1]
OUT = os.path.expanduser("~/eigengs_r5"); os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
RES, NPTS = 256, 20000
ITERS = int(os.environ.get("ITERS", "1000"))
THRESH = [25.0, 30.0, 35.0]
N_IMG = int(os.environ.get("N_IMG", "6"))

arrs = np.load(os.path.join(PARSED, "arrs.npy")); NCOMPS = arrs.shape[0]
gt_arrs = torch.from_numpy(arrs).to(DEV)
with open(os.path.join(PARSED, "pca_object.pkl"), "rb") as f: PCA_OBJ = pickle.load(f)
with open(os.path.join(PARSED, "norm_infos.pkl"), "rb") as f: NORM = pickle.load(f)
FREQ = {"low":[0,50,2000], "high":[50,NCOMPS,NPTS-2000], "all":[0,NCOMPS,NPTS]}
SD = torch.load(CKPT, map_location=DEV, weights_only=True)["model_state_dict"]
MX = np.array([NORM[c]["max"] for c in range(3)]); MN = np.array([NORM[c]["min"] for c in range(3)])

def _from_dir(envvar):
    def f(n):
        root = os.environ.get(envvar, "")
        if not root or not os.path.isdir(root): raise RuntimeError(f"{envvar}={root!r}")
        fs = []
        for e in ("*.png","*.jpg","*.jpeg"): fs += glob.glob(os.path.join(root,"**",e), recursive=True)
        fs = sorted(fs)
        if len(fs) < n: raise RuntimeError(f"{envvar}: {len(fs)} < {n}")
        return [Image.open(p).convert("RGB").resize((RES,RES), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS) for p in fs[:n]]
    return f

def _synth_lineart(n):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1); out=[]
    for _ in range(n):
        im=Image.new("RGB",(RES,RES),(255,255,255)); d=ImageDraw.Draw(im)
        for _ in range(rng.integers(12,20)):
            x0,y0,x1,y1=rng.integers(0,RES,size=4); d.line([int(x0),int(y0),int(x1),int(y1)],fill=(0,0,0),width=2)
        for _ in range(rng.integers(3,7)):
            x0,y0=rng.integers(0,RES-60,size=2); s=rng.integers(30,60)
            d.ellipse([int(x0),int(y0),int(x0+s),int(y0+s)],outline=(0,0,0),width=2)
        out.append(im)
    return out

def to_ycbcr(pil):
    return torch.tensor((color.rgb2ycbcr(pil)/255.0).transpose(2,0,1), dtype=torch.float32, device=DEV)
def psnr(a,b): return 10*math.log10(1.0/F.mse_loss(a.float(),b.float()).item())

def props(gt):
    """Per-image properties on the Y/Cb/Cr planes, as the model sees them."""
    y = gt[0].detach().cpu().numpy()
    cb, cr = gt[1].detach().cpu().numpy(), gt[2].detach().cpu().numpy()
    gy, gx = np.gradient(y)
    edge = float((gy**2 + gx**2).mean() / max(y.var(), 1e-9))
    return {
        "ink_frac":    float((y < 0.35).mean()),
        "white_frac":  float((y > 0.90).mean()),
        "bimodality":  float(((y < 0.35) | (y > 0.90)).mean()),
        "edge_energy": edge,
        "chroma_std":  float(np.sqrt(((cb-0.5)**2 + (cr-0.5)**2).mean())),
        "y_std":       float(y.std()),
    }

def pca_res_psnr(gt):
    a = gt.detach().cpu().numpy().reshape(3,-1)
    rec = np.stack([PCA_OBJ[c].inverse_transform(PCA_OBJ[c].transform(a[c].reshape(1,-1)))[0] for c in range(3)])
    return 10*math.log10(1.0/max(np.mean((rec-a)**2), 1e-12))

def build():
    return GaussianBasis(loss_type="L2", opt_type="adan", num_points=NPTS, H=RES, W=RES,
                         BLOCK_H=16, BLOCK_W=16, device=DEV, lr=1e-3, num_comps=NCOMPS,
                         gt_arrs=gt_arrs, freq_config=FREQ).to(DEV)

def solve_affine(raw, tgt):
    s=torch.empty(3,device=DEV); t=torch.empty(3,device=DEV)
    for c in range(3):
        x,y=raw[c].double(),tgt[c].double(); n=x.numel()
        sxx,sx,sxy,sy=(x*x).sum(),x.sum(),(x*y).sum(),y.sum(); det=sxx*n-sx*sx
        if det.abs()<1e-8: s[c],t[c]=1.0,0.0
        else: s[c]=((sxy*n-sx*sy)/det).float(); t[c]=((sxx*sy-sx*sxy)/det).float()
    return s,t

def project(m, gt):
    m.cur_freq="all"
    a=gt.detach().cpu().numpy().reshape(3,-1)
    codes=np.stack([PCA_OBJ[c].transform(a[c].reshape(1,-1)) for c in range(3)])
    means=np.stack([PCA_OBJ[c].mean_ for c in range(3)])
    ct=torch.tensor(codes,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEV); mt=torch.tensor(means,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEV)
    m.image_mean=mt
    m.shift_factor=ct.sum(dim=2).squeeze(1)*torch.tensor(MN,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEV)
    m.scale_factor=torch.tensor(MX-MN,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEV)
    with torch.no_grad():
        base=torch.bmm(ct,m.get_features.permute(2,0,1)).squeeze(1).transpose(0,1)
        m._colors.copy_(base)
    return base, mt

def init_arm(m, gt, arm):
    if arm=="scratch":
        m.cur_freq="all"
        with torch.no_grad():
            m._colors.uniform_(0.0,1.0)
            m.image_mean=torch.zeros(3,RES*RES,device=DEV)
            m.scale_factor=torch.ones(3,device=DEV); m.shift_factor=torch.zeros(3,device=DEV)
        return m
    base, mt = project(m, gt)
    if arm=="eigengs": return m
    if arm=="absorb":
        with torch.no_grad():
            m.scale_factor=torch.ones(3,device=DEV); m.shift_factor=torch.zeros(3,device=DEV)
            raw=m(render_colors=True).reshape(3,-1)
            s,t=solve_affine(raw, gt.reshape(3,-1)-mt)
            m._colors.copy_(base*s.view(1,3)); m.image_mean=mt+t.view(3,1)
        return m
    raise ValueError(arm)

def render(m):
    with torch.no_grad():
        return (m(render_colors=True).reshape(3,-1)+m.image_mean).reshape(3,RES,RES)

def run(arm, gt):
    m=build()
    if arm!="scratch": m.load_state_dict(SD)
    m=init_arm(m,gt,arm)
    ip=psnr(render(m),gt)
    m.scheduler_init(optimize_phase=True); m.train()
    hit={}
    for it in range(1,ITERS+1):
        _,p=m.optimize_iter(gt)
        for th in THRESH:
            if th not in hit and p>=th: hit[th]=it
    fin=render(m)
    return {"init_psnr":ip,"final_psnr":psnr(fin,gt),"hit":{str(k):v for k,v in hit.items()}}, fin

def save_rgb(t,p):
    y=t.detach().cpu().numpy().transpose(1,2,0)*255.0
    Image.fromarray(np.clip(color.ycbcr2rgb(y)*255.0,0,255).astype(np.uint8)).save(p)

ARMS=["scratch","eigengs","absorb"]
# real line-art sub-types, fetched by the job script into these dirs
EXPS=[("manga_tone",   _from_dir("MANGA_DIR")),     # screentoned manga panels (round 3: WINS)
      ("lineart_pure", _from_dir("PURE_DIR")),      # inked/bilevel line drawings, coloring pages
      ("sketch_pencil",_from_dir("PENCIL_DIR")),    # pencil sketches (grey, soft strokes)
      ("illustration", _from_dir("ILLUST_DIR")),    # flat-colour anime illustration
      ("synth_lineart",_synth_lineart)]             # known end-point of the axis

rows=[]; t0=time.time()
for name, src in EXPS:
    try: imgs=src(N_IMG)
    except Exception as ex:
        print(f"\n=== {name}: SKIPPED ({type(ex).__name__}: {ex})", flush=True); continue
    print(f"\n=== {name}: {len(imgs)} imgs", flush=True)
    for i,pil in enumerate(imgs):
        gt=to_ycbcr(pil); pr=pca_res_psnr(gt); pp=props(gt); cur={}
        for arm in ARMS:
            r,fin=run(arm,gt)
            rows.append(dict(exp=name,idx=i,arm=arm,pca_res=pr,**pp,**r)); cur[arm]=r
            if i<2: save_rgb(gt,f"{OUT}/{name}{i}_gt.png"); save_rgb(fin,f"{OUT}/{name}{i}_{arm}.png")
        d=cur["eigengs"]["final_psnr"]-cur["scratch"]["final_psnr"]
        print(f"  [{i}] ink {pp['ink_frac']:.3f} white {pp['white_frac']:.3f} bimod {pp['bimodality']:.3f} "
              f"edge {pp['edge_energy']:.4f} chroma {pp['chroma_std']:.4f} pca_res {pr:5.1f} "
              f"| eig-scr {d:+6.2f}  ({time.time()-t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
    with open(f"{OUT}/round5.json","w") as f: json.dump(rows,f)

with open(f"{OUT}/round5.json","w") as f: json.dump(rows,f)

print("\n=================== SUMMARY ===================")
for name,_ in EXPS:
    sub=[r for r in rows if r["exp"]==name]
    if not sub: continue
    scr=np.mean([r["final_psnr"] for r in sub if r["arm"]=="scratch"])
    print(f"\n--- {name} (n={len({r['idx'] for r in sub})})  "
          f"ink {np.mean([r['ink_frac'] for r in sub]):.3f}  white {np.mean([r['white_frac'] for r in sub]):.3f}  "
          f"bimod {np.mean([r['bimodality'] for r in sub]):.3f}  chroma {np.mean([r['chroma_std'] for r in sub]):.4f}  "
          f"pca_res {np.mean([r['pca_res'] for r in sub]):.1f}")
    for a in ARMS:
        v=[r["final_psnr"] for r in sub if r["arm"]==a]
        if not v: continue
        print(f"  {a:<9} init {np.mean([r['init_psnr'] for r in sub if r['arm']==a]):6.2f}  "
              f"final {np.mean(v):6.2f}  vs_scratch {np.mean(v)-scr:+6.2f}")

# --- property vs outcome, pooled over every real image -----------------------
per=[]
for name,_ in EXPS:
    for i in sorted({r["idx"] for r in rows if r["exp"]==name}):
        g=[r for r in rows if r["exp"]==name and r["idx"]==i]
        e=[r for r in g if r["arm"]=="eigengs"]; s=[r for r in g if r["arm"]=="scratch"]
        if e and s: per.append({**{k:e[0][k] for k in ("ink_frac","white_frac","bimodality",
                                 "edge_energy","chroma_std","y_std","pca_res")},
                                "exp":name, "adv":e[0]["final_psnr"]-s[0]["final_psnr"]})
print("\n--- correlation of each property with the EigenGS advantage (all images pooled)")
if len(per)>3:
    adv=np.array([p["adv"] for p in per])
    for k in ("ink_frac","white_frac","bimodality","edge_energy","chroma_std","y_std","pca_res"):
        x=np.array([p[k] for p in per])

        print(f"  {k:<12} r = {r:+.3f}")
    real=[p for p in per if p["exp"]!="synth_lineart"]
    if len(real)>3:
        advr=np.array([p["adv"] for p in real])
        print("  --- real images only (synthetic excluded)")
        for k in ("ink_frac","white_frac","bimodality","edge_energy","chroma_std","pca_res"):

"""Round 6 -- PACS: hold the CONTENT fixed, vary only the drawing STYLE.

Every failure comparison so far confounded content with style (manga panels vs
scanned invoices vs synthetic strokes). PACS fixes that: the same seven
categories (dog, elephant, giraffe, guitar, horse, house, person) are provided
in four styles -- photo, art_painting, cartoon, sketch. Evaluating matched
categories across the four styles isolates the style axis, which is exactly the
axis the paper's cross-dataset claim lives on.

Note that manga panels are NOT line art: screentone, filled blacks and speech
bubbles give them a full grey range. PACS `sketch` is the real line-art
condition -- human-drawn thin strokes on white paper.

Arms: scratch / eigengs / absorb, 1000 iterations, ImageNet basis (unchanged).
Per image we also log the properties that could explain the outcome, so the
claim rests on a measured correlate rather than on the domain label.
"""
import os, sys, math, json, time, pickle, glob
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from PIL import Image
from skimage import color

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.expanduser("~/EigenGS"))
os.chdir(os.path.expanduser("~/EigenGS"))
from gaussianbasis import GaussianBasis

DEV = torch.device("cuda:0")
PARSED = os.path.expanduser("~/eigengs_data/5d32e0-300")
CKPT = sorted(glob.glob("./models/multi-freq/5d32e0-300-20000-2000-*/gaussian_model.pth.tar"))[-1]
OUT = os.path.expanduser("~/eigengs_r6"); os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
RES, NPTS = 256, 20000
ITERS = int(os.environ.get("ITERS", "1000"))
THRESH = [25.0, 30.0, 35.0]
PER_STYLE = int(os.environ.get("PER_STYLE", "7"))   # one image per category
PACS = os.environ.get("PACS_DIR", os.path.expanduser("~/pacs"))
STYLES = ["photo", "art_painting", "cartoon", "sketch"]
CATS = ["dog", "elephant", "giraffe", "guitar", "horse", "house", "person"]

arrs = np.load(os.path.join(PARSED, "arrs.npy")); NCOMPS = arrs.shape[0]
gt_arrs = torch.from_numpy(arrs).to(DEV)
with open(os.path.join(PARSED, "pca_object.pkl"), "rb") as f: PCA_OBJ = pickle.load(f)
with open(os.path.join(PARSED, "norm_infos.pkl"), "rb") as f: NORM = pickle.load(f)
FREQ = {"low":[0,50,2000], "high":[50,NCOMPS,NPTS-2000], "all":[0,NCOMPS,NPTS]}
SD = torch.load(CKPT, map_location=DEV, weights_only=True)["model_state_dict"]
MX = np.array([NORM[c]["max"] for c in range(3)]); MN = np.array([NORM[c]["min"] for c in range(3)])

def load_pacs(style):
    """One image per category, so content is matched across styles."""
    out = []
    for cat in CATS[:PER_STYLE]:
        fs = []
        for e in ("*.jpg","*.png","*.jpeg"):
            fs += glob.glob(os.path.join(PACS, style, cat, e))
        if not fs:
            fs = []
            for e in ("*.jpg","*.png","*.jpeg"):
                fs += glob.glob(os.path.join(PACS, "**", style, cat, e), recursive=True)
        if not fs:
            raise RuntimeError(f"no images for {style}/{cat} under {PACS}")
        p = sorted(fs)[0]
        out.append((cat, Image.open(p).convert("RGB").resize((RES,RES), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)))
    return out

def to_ycbcr(pil):
    return torch.tensor((color.rgb2ycbcr(pil)/255.0).transpose(2,0,1), dtype=torch.float32, device=DEV)
def psnr(a,b): return 10*math.log10(1.0/F.mse_loss(a.float(),b.float()).item())

def props(gt):
    y = gt[0].detach().cpu().numpy()
    cb, cr = gt[1].detach().cpu().numpy(), gt[2].detach().cpu().numpy()
    gy, gx = np.gradient(y)
    return {"ink_frac": float((y<0.35).mean()), "white_frac": float((y>0.90).mean()),
            "bimodality": float(((y<0.35)|(y>0.90)).mean()),
            "edge_energy": float((gy**2+gx**2).mean()/max(y.var(),1e-9)),
            "chroma_std": float(np.sqrt(((cb-0.5)**2+(cr-0.5)**2).mean())),
            "y_std": float(y.std())}

def pca_res_psnr(gt):
    a=gt.detach().cpu().numpy().reshape(3,-1)
    rec=np.stack([PCA_OBJ[c].inverse_transform(PCA_OBJ[c].transform(a[c].reshape(1,-1)))[0] for c in range(3)])
    return 10*math.log10(1.0/max(np.mean((rec-a)**2),1e-12))

def build():
    return GaussianBasis(loss_type="L2", opt_type="adan", num_points=NPTS, H=RES, W=RES,
                         BLOCK_H=16, BLOCK_W=16, device=DEV, lr=1e-3, num_comps=NCOMPS,
                         gt_arrs=gt_arrs, freq_config=FREQ).to(DEV)

def solve_affine(raw,tgt):
    s=torch.empty(3,device=DEV); t=torch.empty(3,device=DEV)
    for c in range(3):
        x,y=raw[c].double(),tgt[c].double(); n=x.numel()
        sxx,sx,sxy,sy=(x*x).sum(),x.sum(),(x*y).sum(),y.sum(); det=sxx*n-sx*sx
        if det.abs()<1e-8: s[c],t[c]=1.0,0.0
        else: s[c]=((sxy*n-sx*sy)/det).float(); t[c]=((sxx*sy-sx*sxy)/det).float()
    return s,t

def project(m,gt):
    m.cur_freq="all"
    a=gt.detach().cpu().numpy().reshape(3,-1)
    codes=np.stack([PCA_OBJ[c].transform(a[c].reshape(1,-1)) for c in range(3)])
    means=np.stack([PCA_OBJ[c].mean_ for c in range(3)])
    ct=torch.tensor(codes,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEV); mt=torch.tensor(means,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEV)
    m.image_mean=mt
    m.shift_factor=ct.sum(dim=2).squeeze(1)*torch.tensor(MN,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEV)
    m.scale_factor=torch.tensor(MX-MN,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEV)
    with torch.no_grad():
        base=torch.bmm(ct,m.get_features.permute(2,0,1)).squeeze(1).transpose(0,1)
        m._colors.copy_(base)
    return base,mt

def init_arm(m,gt,arm):
    if arm=="scratch":
        m.cur_freq="all"
        with torch.no_grad():
            m._colors.uniform_(0.0,1.0)
            m.image_mean=torch.zeros(3,RES*RES,device=DEV)
            m.scale_factor=torch.ones(3,device=DEV); m.shift_factor=torch.zeros(3,device=DEV)
        return m
    base,mt=project(m,gt)
    if arm=="eigengs": return m
    if arm=="absorb":
        with torch.no_grad():
            m.scale_factor=torch.ones(3,device=DEV); m.shift_factor=torch.zeros(3,device=DEV)
            raw=m(render_colors=True).reshape(3,-1)
            s,t=solve_affine(raw,gt.reshape(3,-1)-mt)
            m._colors.copy_(base*s.view(1,3)); m.image_mean=mt+t.view(3,1)
        return m
    raise ValueError(arm)

def render(m):
    with torch.no_grad(): return (m(render_colors=True).reshape(3,-1)+m.image_mean).reshape(3,RES,RES)

def run(arm,gt):
    m=build()
    if arm!="scratch": m.load_state_dict(SD)
    m=init_arm(m,gt,arm)
    ip=psnr(render(m),gt)
    m.scheduler_init(optimize_phase=True); m.train()
    hit={}
    for it in range(1,ITERS+1):
        _,p=m.optimize_iter(gt)
        for th in THRESH:
            if th not in hit and p>=th: hit[th]=it
    fin=render(m)
    return {"init_psnr":ip,"final_psnr":psnr(fin,gt),"hit":{str(k):v for k,v in hit.items()}},fin

def save_rgb(t,p):
    y=t.detach().cpu().numpy().transpose(1,2,0)*255.0
    Image.fromarray(np.clip(color.ycbcr2rgb(y)*255.0,0,255).astype(np.uint8)).save(p)

ARMS=["scratch","eigengs","absorb"]
rows=[]; t0=time.time()
for style in STYLES:
    try: imgs=load_pacs(style)
    except Exception as ex:
        print(f"\n=== {style}: SKIPPED ({type(ex).__name__}: {ex})", flush=True); continue
    print(f"\n=== {style}: {len(imgs)} imgs (one per category)", flush=True)
    for i,(cat,pil) in enumerate(imgs):
        gt=to_ycbcr(pil); pr=pca_res_psnr(gt); pp=props(gt); cur={}
        for arm in ARMS:
            r,fin=run(arm,gt)
            rows.append(dict(style=style,cat=cat,idx=i,arm=arm,pca_res=pr,**pp,**r)); cur[arm]=r
            if i<2: save_rgb(gt,f"{OUT}/{style}_{cat}_gt.png"); save_rgb(fin,f"{OUT}/{style}_{cat}_{arm}.png")
        d=cur["eigengs"]["final_psnr"]-cur["scratch"]["final_psnr"]
        da=cur["absorb"]["final_psnr"]-cur["scratch"]["final_psnr"]
        print(f"  {cat:<9} ink {pp['ink_frac']:.3f} white {pp['white_frac']:.3f} bimod {pp['bimodality']:.3f} "
              f"chroma {pp['chroma_std']:.4f} pca_res {pr:5.1f} | eig {d:+6.2f}  absorb {da:+6.2f} "
              f"({time.time()-t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
    with open(f"{OUT}/round6.json","w") as f: json.dump(rows,f)

with open(f"{OUT}/round6.json","w") as f: json.dump(rows,f)

print("\n============ SUMMARY: same categories, four styles ============")
for style in STYLES:
    sub=[r for r in rows if r["style"]==style]
    if not sub: continue
    scr=np.mean([r["final_psnr"] for r in sub if r["arm"]=="scratch"])
    print(f"\n--- {style} (n={len({r['idx'] for r in sub})})  ink {np.mean([r['ink_frac'] for r in sub]):.3f} "
          f"white {np.mean([r['white_frac'] for r in sub]):.3f} bimod {np.mean([r['bimodality'] for r in sub]):.3f} "
          f"chroma {np.mean([r['chroma_std'] for r in sub]):.4f} pca_res {np.mean([r['pca_res'] for r in sub]):.1f}")
    for a in ARMS:
        v=[r["final_psnr"] for r in sub if r["arm"]==a]
        if not v: continue
        h=[r["hit"].get("30.0") for r in sub if r["arm"]==a and r["hit"].get("30.0")]
        print(f"  {a:<9} init {np.mean([r['init_psnr'] for r in sub if r['arm']==a]):6.2f} "
              f"final {np.mean(v):6.2f}  vs_scratch {np.mean(v)-scr:+6.2f}  "

    idxs=sorted({r["idx"] for r in sub})

    print(f"  images where EigenGS is worse than random: {worse}/{len(idxs)}")

hdr = "  " + "cat".ljust(10) + "".join(s[:9].rjust(11) for s in STYLES)

数値が裏付けました。`Chan-Y/Manga-Drawings` のサンプルは**インク率 89.6%** — 画像の9割が暗部で、白地は 4.6% しかありません。線画どころか、ほぼ全面が黒の切り絵状の画像です。対する合成線画はインク率 8.7%、白地 91.3%、エッジエネルギー 0.64(漫画の 0.20 の3倍)。

**両者は「疎な線 vs 密な面」で正反対**でした。私が「実データ線画では勝つ」と報告したのは誤りで、勝っていたのは面の絵です。これで矛盾は消えます — 疎な細線という条件では、合成でも実データでも壊れる可能性が高い。PACS sketch でそれを実データで確かめます。

cat > fetch_pacs.py <<'EOF'
"""Fetch PACS (photo / art_painting / cartoon / sketch, 7 shared categories).

PACS is a domain-generalisation benchmark, so the same categories exist in all
four styles -- that is what makes the style axis separable from content. Try the
HF datasets-server first (several public mirrors), then fall back to a direct
parquet/zip download if one is exposed.
"""
import sys, os, io, json, urllib.request, urllib.parse

OUT = sys.argv[1]; PER = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 7
STYLES = ["photo", "art_painting", "cartoon", "sketch"]
CATS = ["dog", "elephant", "giraffe", "guitar", "horse", "house", "person"]
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

def get(u, t=90):
    return urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(
        u, headers={"Accept": "application/json"}), t).read()

def search(term, limit=30):
    u = ("https://huggingface.co/api/datasets?search=%s&sort=downloads&direction=-1&limit=%d"
         % (urllib.parse.quote(term), limit))
    try:
        return [d["id"] for d in json.loads(get(u))]
    except Exception as e:
        print("  search err", type(e).__name__, flush=True); return []

cands = []
for t in ("PACS", "pacs domain generalization", "domainnet sketch", "domain generalization pacs"):
    for d in search(t):
        if d not in cands: cands.append(d)
print("candidates:", json.dumps(cands[:25]), flush=True)

from PIL import Image

def norm_style(v):
    s = str(v).lower().replace(" ", "_")
    for st in STYLES:
        if st in s or s in st: return st
    if "art" in s and "paint" in s: return "art_painting"
    return None

def norm_cat(v):
    s = str(v).lower()
    for c in CATS:
        if c in s: return c
    return None

def try_ds(ds):
    """Walk the rows API, bucketing by (style, category) until each has PER."""
    q = urllib.parse.quote(ds, safe="")
    try:
        info = json.loads(get("https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/splits?dataset=" + q))
    except Exception as e:
        return 0, "splits:" + type(e).__name__
    got = {}
    for sp in info["splits"]:
        cfg, spl = sp["config"], sp["split"]
        # the config name itself often IS the style in PACS mirrors
        cfg_style = norm_style(cfg) or norm_style(spl)
        for off in range(0, 3000, 100):
            url = ("https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/rows?dataset=%s&config=%s&split=%s"
                   "&offset=%d&length=100" % (q, urllib.parse.quote(cfg, safe=""),
                                              urllib.parse.quote(spl, safe=""), off))
            try:
                rows = json.loads(get(url, 120)).get("rows", [])
            except Exception:
                break
            if not rows: break
            for r in rows:
                row = r["row"]
                style = cfg_style; cat = None; src = None
                for k, v in row.items():
                    kl = k.lower()
                    if isinstance(v, dict) and "src" in v: src = v["src"]
                    elif "domain" in kl or "style" in kl:  style = norm_style(v) or style
                    elif "label" in kl or "class" in kl or "categ" in kl: cat = norm_cat(v) or cat
                    elif isinstance(v, str) and "/" in v:
                        style = style or norm_style(v.split("/")[0]); cat = cat or norm_cat(v)
                if not (src and style and cat): continue
                key = (style, cat)
                if len(got.get(key, [])) >= PER: continue
                try:
                    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(urllib.request.urlopen(src, timeout=90).read())).convert("RGB")
                except Exception:
                    continue
                if min(im.size) < 96: return 0, "too small %s" % (im.size,)
                d = os.path.join(OUT, style, cat); os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
                im.save(os.path.join(d, "img_%02d.png" % len(got.get(key, []))))
                got.setdefault(key, []).append(1)
            full = sum(1 for s in STYLES for c in CATS if len(got.get((s, c), [])) >= PER)
            if full >= len(STYLES) * len(CATS): break
        print("    %s/%s -> %d buckets filled" % (cfg, spl,
              sum(1 for s in STYLES for c in CATS if len(got.get((s,c),[])) >= PER)), flush=True)
    have = {s: sum(1 for c in CATS if len(got.get((s,c),[])) >= 1) for s in STYLES}
    print("    per-style categories:", have, flush=True)
    return min(have.values()) if have else 0, "ok"

best = 0
for ds in cands[:10]:
    print("--- trying", ds, flush=True)
    n, msg = try_ds(ds)
    print("    => %d cats/style (%s)" % (n, msg), flush=True)
    if n >= 5:
        json.dump({"dataset": ds, "cats_per_style": n}, open(os.path.join(OUT, "_source.json"), "w"))
        best = n; break
print("PACS RESULT cats_per_style=%d" % best, flush=True)
for s in STYLES:
    d = os.path.join(OUT, s)
    print("  %-14s %d files" % (s, sum(len(f) for _,_,f in os.walk(d)) if os.path.isdir(d) else 0))
sys.exit(0 if best >= 5 else 3)

# ---- improvement arms aimed at the sparse-line condition --------------------
# Mechanism: the PCA mean Psi_0 is a natural-image mean (mid-grey); a sketch is
# ~0.95 white with sparse dark strokes. The init must drag the whole canvas to
# white using a basis built for mid-grey content. Two fixes, both per-image and
# training-free:
#   dcfix    : replace Psi_0 with the image's OWN dc level, so the Gaussians only
#              have to represent the strokes (the deviation), not the paper.
#   lumc_k   : compress the luminance range toward the basis' trained range
#              before projecting, then let optimisation recover contrast --
#              the luminance analogue of the chroma trick that worked on
#              saturated images.
src = src.replace('''def init_arm(m,gt,arm):''',
'''def dc_of(gt):
    """Per-channel DC level of this image, as a broadcastable mean image."""
    return gt.reshape(3,-1).mean(dim=1, keepdim=True).expand(3, RES*RES).contiguous()

def compress_luma(gt, k):
    """Pull the Y range toward its own mean by factor k; chroma untouched.
    Linear in Y, so it is exactly invertible -- but we do not invert it: the
    optimiser recovers the true contrast from a better-conditioned start."""
    out = gt.clone()
    mu = out[0].mean()
    out[0] = (out[0] - mu)*k + mu
    return out

def init_arm(m,gt,arm):''')

src = src.replace('''    if arm=="absorb":
        with torch.no_grad():
            m.scale_factor=torch.ones(3,device=DEV); m.shift_factor=torch.zeros(3,device=DEV)
            raw=m(render_colors=True).reshape(3,-1)
            s,t=solve_affine(raw,gt.reshape(3,-1)-mt)
            m._colors.copy_(base*s.view(1,3)); m.image_mean=mt+t.view(3,1)
        return m
    raise ValueError(arm)''',
'''    if arm=="absorb":
        with torch.no_grad():
            m.scale_factor=torch.ones(3,device=DEV); m.shift_factor=torch.zeros(3,device=DEV)
            raw=m(render_colors=True).reshape(3,-1)
            s,t=solve_affine(raw,gt.reshape(3,-1)-mt)
            m._colors.copy_(base*s.view(1,3)); m.image_mean=mt+t.view(3,1)
        return m
    if arm=="dcfix":
        # paper stays paper: mean image is this image's own DC, not the PCA mean
        with torch.no_grad():
            dc=dc_of(gt)
            m.scale_factor=torch.ones(3,device=DEV); m.shift_factor=torch.zeros(3,device=DEV)
            raw=m(render_colors=True).reshape(3,-1)
            s,t=solve_affine(raw, gt.reshape(3,-1)-dc)
            m._colors.copy_(base*s.view(1,3)); m.image_mean=dc+t.view(3,1)
        return m
    if arm.startswith("lumc"):
        k=float(arm.split("_")[1])
        base2,mt2=project(m, compress_luma(gt,k))
        with torch.no_grad():
            m.scale_factor=torch.ones(3,device=DEV); m.shift_factor=torch.zeros(3,device=DEV)

            m._colors.copy_(base2*s.view(1,3)); m.image_mean=mt2+t.view(3,1)
        return m

切り分けが決着しました。**私が疑っていた実効学習率の交絡は否定され、勾配経路が原因で確定です**。

| 対照 | 効果 |
|---|---|
| `fold_repo`(リポジトリ自身の定数を色に畳み込む。初期画像は `eigengs` と数学的に同一) | **+5.3〜+15.3 dB** |
| `eigengs_lr`(バッファはそのまま、色の学習率だけ 1/scale 倍) | +0.1〜+3.6 dB のみ |
| `absorb_lr`(畳み込んだ上で学習率を打ち消す) | 効果消失(−7.1〜+8.3) |

決定的なのは `fold_repo`: **初期画像を1ピクセルも変えず、`scale_factor` をバッファから色パラメータへ移すだけで全7ドメインが改善**。単なる学習率調整(`eigengs_lr`)では再現しないので、実効ステップサイズの話ではありません。勾配の実測値も裏付けています — 反復1での `|grad|` が `eigengs` の 1.07e-07 に対し `fold_repo` は 2.61e-06(約24倍、`max-min` の逆数に一致)。固定バッファが勾配を潰していました。

10000反復の結果も確認します。

cat > fetch_styles.py <<'EOF'
"""Fetch a style-axis corpus (PACS or DomainNet) and report exactly what it found.

The previous attempt searched HF for "PACS" and got 0 usable images -- most
likely because "PACS" also names a physical-audiovisual-commonsense VQA dataset,
so the search hits were the wrong PACS. This version targets concrete dataset
ids, prints each candidate's splits and row schema, and fetches from the first
one that actually carries a style/domain field plus images.

Layout written: <out>/<style>/<category>/img_NN.png
"""
import sys, os, io, json, urllib.request, urllib.parse

OUT = sys.argv[1]
PER = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 1
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

CANDS = [
    # (dataset id, note)
    "flwrlabs/pacs",
    "Ramos-Ramos/pacs",
    "nateraw/pacs",
    "kowndinya23/pacs",
    "HichTala/PACS",
    "wltjr1007/DomainNet",
    "Chris1/DomainNet",
    "wanghaofan/domainnet",
]
PACS_STYLES = ["photo", "art_painting", "cartoon", "sketch"]
DN_STYLES = ["real", "painting", "clipart", "sketch"]

def get(u, t=90):
    return urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(
        u, headers={"Accept": "application/json"}), t).read()

from PIL import Image

def probe(ds):
    q = urllib.parse.quote(ds, safe="")
    try:
        info = json.loads(get("https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/splits?dataset=" + q))
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  {ds:<26} splits FAILED {type(e).__name__}", flush=True)
        return None
    splits = info.get("splits", [])
    print(f"  {ds:<26} splits: {[(s['config'], s['split']) for s in splits][:6]}", flush=True)
    if not splits:
        return None
    sp = splits[0]
    url = ("https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/rows?dataset=%s&config=%s&split=%s&offset=0&length=3"
           % (q, urllib.parse.quote(sp["config"], safe=""), urllib.parse.quote(sp["split"], safe="")))
    try:
        rows = json.loads(get(url, 120)).get("rows", [])
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"      rows FAILED {type(e).__name__}", flush=True); return None
    if not rows:
        print("      rows empty", flush=True); return None
    row = rows[0]["row"]
    schema = {k: (("IMG" if (isinstance(v, dict) and "src" in v) else type(v).__name__),
                  (str(v)[:40] if not isinstance(v, dict) else "")) for k, v in row.items()}
    print(f"      schema: {schema}", flush=True)
    return {"splits": splits, "schema": list(row.keys())}

def norm(v, vocab):
    s = str(v).lower().replace(" ", "_").replace("-", "_")
    for t in vocab:
        if t == s or t in s: return t
    if "art" in s and "paint" in s: return "art_painting"
    return None

def harvest(ds, info, styles):
    """Walk rows, bucket by (style, category)."""
    q = urllib.parse.quote(ds, safe="")
    got = {}
    for sp in info["splits"]:
        cfg, spl = sp["config"], sp["split"]
        cfg_style = norm(cfg, styles) or norm(spl, styles)
        for off in range(0, 4000, 100):
            url = ("https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/rows?dataset=%s&config=%s&split=%s"
                   "&offset=%d&length=100" % (q, urllib.parse.quote(cfg, safe=""),
                                              urllib.parse.quote(spl, safe=""), off))
            try:
                rows = json.loads(get(url, 120)).get("rows", [])
            except Exception:
                break
            if not rows: break
            for r in rows:
                row = r["row"]; style = cfg_style; cat = None; src = None
                for k, v in row.items():
                    kl = k.lower()
                    if isinstance(v, dict) and "src" in v: src = v["src"]
                    elif "domain" in kl or "style" in kl: style = norm(v, styles) or style
                    elif "label" in kl or "class" in kl or "categ" in kl: cat = str(v)
                if not (src and style): continue
                cat = (cat or "all")[:24].replace("/", "_")
                key = (style, cat)
                if len(got.get(key, [])) >= PER: continue
                try:
                    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(urllib.request.urlopen(src, timeout=90).read())).convert("RGB")
                except Exception:
                    continue
                if min(im.size) < 96: return {}, "too small %s" % (im.size,)
                d = os.path.join(OUT, style, cat); os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
                im.save(os.path.join(d, "img_%02d.png" % len(got.get(key, []))))
                got.setdefault(key, []).append(1)
            per_style = {s: len({c for (st, c) in got if st == s}) for s in styles}
            if all(per_style.get(s, 0) >= 5 for s in styles): break
        print(f"      after {cfg}/{spl}: " +
              str({s: len({c for (st, c) in got if st == s}) for s in styles}), flush=True)
        if all(len({c for (st, c) in got if st == s}) >= 5 for s in styles): break
    return got, "ok"

chosen = None
for ds in CANDS:
    info = probe(ds)
    if not info: continue
    styles = DN_STYLES if "domainnet" in ds.lower() else PACS_STYLES
    got, msg = harvest(ds, info, styles)
    per_style = {s: len({c for (st, c) in got if st == s}) for s in styles}
    print(f"      -> {ds}: {per_style} ({msg})", flush=True)
    if sum(1 for s in styles if per_style.get(s, 0) >= 3) >= 3:
        chosen = {"dataset": ds, "styles": styles, "per_style": per_style}
        break

print("STYLE_FETCH_RESULT", json.dumps(chosen), flush=True)
json.dump(chosen or {}, open(os.path.join(OUT, "_source.json"), "w"))
for root, dirs, files in os.walk(OUT):
    png = [f for f in files if f.endswith(".png")]
    if png: print("  %-50s %d" % (os.path.relpath(root, OUT), len(png)))
sys.exit(0 if chosen else 3)
